display.text: Stage assigning each observation to the cluster whose current centroid is nearest.
Vector of coordinate-wise means of the observations assigned to a cluster. Also called cluster center.
Choice of starting cluster centers before the assignment and update iterations; different starts may produce different solutions.
Grouping observations so that members of a group are similar according to selected features and a chosen similarity measure. Also called cluster analysis.
Stabilization of assignments or centroids, or negligible further improvement in the objective; it does not ensure the best possible clustering.
Rule for quantifying how far apart observations are; standard k-means uses Euclidean distance for assignment.
Heuristic choosing k near a bend in the plot of WCSS against cluster number, after which additional clusters yield smaller improvements.
Straight-line distance between vectors, calculated as the square root of the sum of squared differences in their coordinates.
Solution with the smallest objective value among all possible clusterings for the specified k and criterion.
Method partitioning observations into k groups by alternating assignment to the nearest centroid and recomputation of cluster means, seeking to minimize within-cluster squared distances.
Solution that cannot be improved by the algorithm's nearby updates but may have a worse objective value than another solution.
Repeated k-means fits from different initial centers, retaining a good solution to reduce dependence on a single initialization. In the R example, nstart specifies the number of starts.
Numerical criterion optimized by an algorithm; for k-means it is the total within-cluster sum of squares.
Dependence of clustering results on feature measurement scales because large-scale coordinates can dominate distance calculations.
Evaluation of how well observations fit their own clusters relative to other clusters; larger silhouette scores suggest better-separated groups.
Learning patterns or groups from features without fitting to a supplied target outcome or class label.
Stage recomputing each centroid as the mean of observations currently assigned to that cluster.
Total squared Euclidean distance from each observation to its assigned centroid; the objective minimized by standard k-means. Also called inertia and abbreviated WCSS or WSS.
